IDEAL-001.predicate: Endpoint discovery returns a connectable address, transport kind, and environment override on Linux, macOS, and Windows without treating a marker file as a live socket.
IDEAL-001.reason: Ovis must connect without platform-specific path guessing.

IDEAL-002.predicate: The handshake returns authenticated machine identity, runtime lifetime, control-server boot ID, protocol generation, methods, capabilities, and negotiated limits.
IDEAL-002.reason: A bridge restart must not masquerade as a new terminal lifetime.

IDEAL-003.predicate: An unsupported protocol generation produces `unsupported_generation` before any state-changing request can run.
IDEAL-003.reason: Incompatible peers must fail at a defined boundary.

IDEAL-004.predicate: One established connection accepts concurrent correlated RPCs, subscription changes, and terminal channels until an explicit close or transport failure.
IDEAL-004.reason: Reusing a connection must not discard later requests.

IDEAL-005.predicate: Every accepted RPC request has a unique string ID and receives exactly one terminal result or structured error with that same ID while the connection remains writable.
IDEAL-005.reason: Interleaved traffic must not be mistaken for another call's answer.

IDEAL-006.predicate: Incremental frame decoding produces identical records for every fragmentation or coalescing of valid input bytes, with JSON control and terminal bytes on distinct channels.
IDEAL-006.reason: Socket read boundaries cannot define application messages.

IDEAL-007.predicate: A negotiated frame is at most 16 MiB, and paginated or chunked reads can return at least 64 MiB logical results with explicit total, continuation, and truncation fields.
IDEAL-007.reason: Large reads need bounded transport without silent data loss.

IDEAL-008.predicate: Every malformed method or parameter, including an unknown targeting field, is rejected before dispatch with a stable kind and offending field path.
IDEAL-008.reason: Ignored arguments must never select the focused pane.

IDEAL-009.predicate: Every target-sensitive call requires a typed resource ID or an explicitly requested caller binding, and ambiguous names return structured candidates without acting.
IDEAL-009.reason: Automation must never inherit an unrelated human selection.

IDEAL-010.predicate: Every RPC has a caller-visible deadline, defaulting to 10 seconds, and long-running work returns a queryable operation ID before that deadline.
IDEAL-010.reason: Worktree and remote operations must not hold an ordinary call indefinitely.

IDEAL-011.predicate: Cancellation yields `cancelled_before_commit`, `already_committed` with a receipt, or a queryable pending outcome and never claims to undo committed effects.
IDEAL-011.reason: Disconnect and cancellation must not invite unsafe retries.

IDEAL-012.predicate: Mutations accept an operation ID whose result is retained for the advertised deduplication window, and an expired ID cannot be silently replayed as new work.
IDEAL-012.reason: A lost reply must not duplicate input or resource creation.

IDEAL-013.predicate: Errors contain a stable kind, message, recovery hint, retryability, target identity when known, and an operation ID whenever effects may have begun.

IDEAL-015.predicate: Subscription startup returns a subscription ID and snapshot at revision R, followed only by matching changes committed after R.

IDEAL-017.predicate: State snapshots and events share a monotonic sequence domain per runtime lifetime, and stale snapshot revisions are explicitly distinguishable.

IDEAL-018.predicate: Adding, replacing, or removing a subscription filter is acknowledged with an effective sequence and preserves all unaffected subscriptions.
IDEAL-018.reason: A second subscribe must not kill the first stream.

IDEAL-019.predicate: Reconnect with a retained cursor replays subsequent matching events, otherwise returning `missed` with a fresh snapshot and its sequence.

IDEAL-020.predicate: Each subscription emits a heartbeat within 15 seconds of idle time on every supported transport, carrying its current sequence and runtime identity.

IDEAL-021.predicate: Slow subscriptions have advertised queue bounds and receive loss or close state recoverable on reconnect even when the final error frame could not be delivered.

IDEAL-022.predicate: Filtering exposes an acknowledged scan cursor, so sequence gaps caused by nonmatching events are distinguishable from delivery loss.

IDEAL-025.predicate: Completion events carry agent/session identity, turn ID, finish generation, and outcome, with the same values recoverable from snapshots.

IDEAL-026.predicate: A newly registered state wait first evaluates current state and then subscribes atomically, returning immediately when already satisfied.

IDEAL-027.predicate: Under the declared local service profile, committed status and lifecycle changes reach a writable subscribed connection within 100 ms without polling.

IDEAL-028.predicate: Attach returns a structured ready, held, refused, recovering, or ended result, including terminal generation, stream ID, geometry, and reason.
